_note: Difficulty scaling (config/difficulty.rs). scaling: per difficulty, extra director team members, the inspect-odds scale (peek odds come from data/peek.json) and the pounce table id of data/hard_abilities.json ('' = none). depth: per difficulty, the danger by level number (level 1 is the base): hunter speed grows speed_per_level per level up to speed_cap, one extra hunter every extra_every levels up to max_extra, and the safe-room odds fall from safe_room_base by safe_room_per_level down to safe_room_min. Standard is flat (speed 1.0, no extra hunters, the shipped safe-room base 0.055 of world/route/danger.rs SAFE_ROOM_BASE_CHANCE), so Standard plays as before. meter (optional; absent = the shipped defaults, no schema break): the HUD danger meter (Infinite only). It is a ROUTE BASE by depth/difficulty (Difficulty::route_danger) that a nearby alert hunter SPIKES toward 100% (Game::danger). route = depth_weight*depth_t + speed_weight*speed_t + hunters_weight*hunters_t + safe_weight*safe_t (weights sum to 1), where depth_t ramps to 1 at depth_full, speed_t/hunters_t/safe_t normalise this difficulty's speed_scale / extra_hunters / lost safe-room odds by speed_ref/hunters_ref/safe_ref; base = max(route*base_cap, base_min). The spike_* are the nearest-hunter readout's constants (state weight chase/hunt/idle + up to spike_prox within spike_range cells); they reproduce the pre-meter numbers exactly. danger() = min(1, base + (1-base)*spike), so a point-blank chaser pins 100% on any depth/difficulty.
